name: Oliver Heaviside
summary: Victorian electrical engineer, physicist and mathematician known for electromagnetic theory and operational calculus.

summary: Author of this document, Department of Engineering, Durham University.

summary: Author of this document, School of Engineering, Newcastle University.

name: Durham University
summary: University in Durham, UK, affiliation of Christopher Donaghy-Spargo.

name: Newcastle University
summary: University in Newcastle upon Tyne, UK, affiliation of Alex Yakovlev.

name: Royal Society
summary: Learned society for science, Heaviside elected Fellow in 1891.

name: University of Göttingen
summary: German university, conferred honorary doctorate on Heaviside in 1905.

name: Institution of Electrical Engineers
summary: Professional body for electrical engineers, awarded Heaviside Fellowship and Faraday Medal, purchased his papers.

name: Great Northern Telegraph Company
summary: Telegraph company, Heaviside's only paid employer.

name: The Electrician Printing and Publishing Co
summary: Publisher of Heaviside's Electromagnetic Theory volumes.

name: James Clerk Maxwell
summary: Physicist whose electromagnetic theory Heaviside reformulated.

name: G. F. C. Searle
summary: Lifelong friend of Heaviside, wrote personal biography, collaborator.

name: H. J. Josephs
summary: GPO Research Engineer, wrote unpublished biography of Heaviside.

name: Torquay
summary: Town in England where Heaviside died.

name: Newcastle upon Tyne
summary: City in England where Heaviside lived and worked in 1873.

name: London
summary: Capital city, location of The Electrician publisher.

name: Newton Abbot
summary: Town in England, location of Heaviside's old house.

summary: First volume of Heaviside's Electromagnetic Theory, published 1893.

name: Electromagnetic Theory Volume II
summary: Second volume of Heaviside's Electromagnetic Theory, published 1899.

summary: Third volume of Heaviside's Electromagnetic Theory, published 1912.
